direction.comments: The direction on a macro scale is less ambitious compared to the first movie, as it feels more like a standard Bollywood action film, though there are moments where it feels grand and epic; The direction on a micro scale is better this time around, as the interpersonal scenes show the weight of the stakes for this mission and how much it affects Hamza; The storytelling is definitely more focused this time around, as there are clear motives for the protagonist and the plot is more forward-driven to meet continuously rising stakes; It builds tension more through your emotional investment in the characters, as the film is less reliant on action sequences to build tension

performance.comments: Is given more material to work with this time around as he shows the much the toll this mission takes on him physically and mentally as you see why he does what he does; has better chemistry with the cast as you can clearly see his motives and connections to those around him
Basically the same as the first movie, enjoyed his performance as he makes his scenes memorable; feels like he is given less of an impactful role this time around though

cast.comments: Same as the first movie: all the supporting performances kinda mold into each other as nobody really does that much to stand out and be differentiable; despite the lack of unique performances, the cast does work well together in helping move the story forward

story.comments: The concept continues the story from the first movie, showing Hamza's motivations and him battling his inner demons as he tries to complete his mission for his country; The plot structure is linear and focused, but it is just way too long; Character writing is good this time around, as you really get to know Hamza and what drives him, with the stakes of this mission taking a toll on him

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is standard for a Bollywood action film but possesses emotional weight in the interpersonal scenes; The symbolism is once again propaganda, as they continue to ask the question, "What if all Pakistanis are terrorists?" but it is less overt this time around, as the film is more focused on the personal conflict within Hamza; The foreshadowing is less strong than in the last movie because you can predict and guess what is going to happen

score.comments: The score continues to build on themes from the first movie, as it helps make the movie memorable and builds tension in the action sequences

soundtrack.comments: While there is less of an emphasis on the soundtrack compared to the first movie, there are still some good songs that are memorable, as they help make this feel like an action Bollywood film

cinematography.comments: The cinematography is definitely less ambitious than the first movie, but it still helps build the world and the action sequences

editing.comments: The editing helps put together the action sequences but is also less polished than the first movie

sound.comments: The sound helps bring the action sequences to life

visual_effects.comments: The visual effects are definitely less ambitious than the first movie, as it feels like they received too many complaints about the gore and violence in the first film; Despite its drop in quality, it still helps depict the action sequences

production_design.comments: The production design continues to build the world and Karachi

makeup.comments: The makeup is better than in the first movie but is fine overall; The issues from the first movie cannot be corrected without creating continuity errors

review.pacing: Pacing is not as big of an issue because the movie does not really feel like it drags as much as the first movie, but the issue is that this film is unnecessarily long
review.climax: The climax is entertaining but feels less ambitious than the first movie; The ending does a good job of bringing closure to the story
review.tone: The tone is still that of an espionage film but feels more like a drama with its focus on Hamza's internal conflict; The movie still relies on Bollywood tropes in its action sequences
review.overall: Overall, "Dhurandar: The Revenge" trades ambition for focus, as this movie loses a lot of its magic from the first film by foregoing its unique and ambitious world-building and technical elements to tell a more focused story about Hamza's personal journey and how the escalating stakes of the mission take a toll on him; while this movie is still entertaining, it's still political propaganda, even though it is less overt about it this time around
